دَوْمَةٌ n. un. of دَوْمٌ. (M, TA.) [Also, app., as in the present day, and as appears from what follows, A single fruit of the tree called دَوْم.] ―
-b2- And (assumed tropical:) A testicle; (K;) as being likened to the fruit of the دَوْم. (TA.) ―
-b3- [Golius also explains it, as on the authority of the K, as meaning “ Ebriosa mulier; ” and Freytag, as meaning “ mulier vinum vendens: ” both are wrong: it is mentioned in the K as the name of a woman who sold wine.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
